title: Jollof Rice with Fried Plantains and Dressed Greens
summary: West African-style jollof: basmati rice steamed in a reduced purée of charred red peppers, tomato, Scotch bonnet and ginger with deeply cooked tomato paste and spices, finished with butter. Served with crisp fried ripe plantains and a lemony butter-lettuce salad.
notes: Video: 'Perfect Peri Peri Chicken at Home' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Written recipe for the same dish: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/the-best-chicken-and-rice-peri-peri-jollof-recipes ('The Best Chicken and Rice (Peri Peri & Jollof)'). The page lists 'Jollof Rice, Plantains and Salad' as its own recipe: serves 6-8 (we use 6, the low end), prep 25 min, active time 1 hour. The peri peri chicken it is served with is a separate file (peri-peri-chicken-joshua-weissman). Prep 25 min is the page's; cook 60 min is the page's active time, which fits the video (reduce the purée, about 15 minutes of sautéing, 30-35 minutes covered), so times_basis is estimated. The video states the jollof amounts; from the written recipe: 5 cups of greens and 2 Tbsp olive oil for the salad (the video says butter lettuce and 'a little bit' of olive oil). Our estimates: 2-inch knob of ginger 25 g; Scotch bonnets 12 g each; Knorr chicken bouillon cubes 10 g each (cube sizes vary by market; this drives much of the sodium); peeled large plantains 220 g each; small salt amounts (1/4 tsp for the onion, 1/2 tsp for the plantains, 1/4 tsp flaky salt for the salad). Ranges: plantain oil 1/3-1/2 cup, we use 1/3 (the page also says 1/3). The plantains are shallow-fried and drained on paper towels, so their oil is treated as frying oil: not counted, with absorbed oil at 10% of the plantains' raw weight (house rule). The 1/3 cup oil in the rice stays in the dish and is counted. The optional 3 Tbsp butter is counted because he folds it into the rice on camera (house rule 11). Not counted: the two whole bay leaves simmered in the rice (not eaten). Red onion uses USDA 'Onions, raw', and Scotch bonnet USDA red hot chili, as proxies (see new_h3.csv). Basmati uses the existing long-grain white rice record.

steps.text: Pepper paste: char the red bell peppers all over (flame, torch or broiler), steam them in a covered bowl 2-3 minutes, then wipe off the skins with a damp paper towel (don't rinse them) and remove most of the seeds.
Blend the peppers with the halved tomatoes, half the red onion, the Scotch bonnets (seeds in) and the ginger, starting low and working up to high, until very smooth.
Pour into a 4-quart saucepan, bring to a boil over medium-high, then simmer over medium until reduced to about 1 1/2 cups.

Dice the other half onion and roughly chop the garlic. Heat the oil in a 5-6 quart sauté pan or pot over medium, add the onion, garlic and a touch of salt, and cook, stirring often, 4-6 minutes until lightly browned.

Stir in the tomato paste and cook over medium, stirring often, 4-5 minutes until dark and deeply caramelized. Add the salt, thyme, curry powder, crumbled bouillon cubes and smoked paprika and toast about 20 seconds.
Stir in the reduced pepper paste, then the water and chicken stock, until smooth. Bring to a boil over medium-high.

Rinse the basmati in several changes of water until it runs clear. Stir it into the pot, spreading it evenly, and tuck in the bay leaves. Return to a gentle simmer, cover with foil and a lid, and cook over medium-low 25 minutes, then over low 5-10 minutes more.

Plantains: peel and slice on the diagonal about 1/2 inch thick. Heat the oil in a large cast-iron skillet over medium until very hot, then fry in a single layer 2-3 minutes per side until deep golden. Drain on paper towels and salt right away.
Uncover the rice and fluff it, scraping up any crispy bits from the bottom. If you like, gently fold in the cubed butter until melted.
Salad: toss the butter lettuce with a little flaky salt, the olive oil and the lemon juice until lightly coated.
Serve a generous mound of jollof with the plantains and salad, alongside the peri peri chicken.
